# Adaptive Workout Coach

Adaptive Workout Coach is a private, self-hosted web app: a guided 30-minute
workout anyone can follow, done three times per week — even with no routine,
no plan, and no experience. It walks the user through 12 exercises with a
server-backed session timer, per-exercise checklists, demo videos, and a
weekly gym calendar. It is built to grow into a personalized full-body
training companion.

## Who it's for

Anyone who wants a workout to simply follow: people with nothing else to do
who want something structured, and people with no knowledge of how to train
who want the guesswork removed. Every exercise tells the user exactly what to
do, in what order, with big legible dose labels (sets x reps), muscle-group
tags, and demo video links where verified demos exist. No expertise required.

## What the app does

- Runs a guided 30-minute workout session: warm-up (4 min), strength (18 min),
  stability (5 min), cool-down (3 min) — 12 exercises built around dumbbells
  and a resistance band.
- Tracks each exercise with a checkbox, a large dose label, muscle-group tags,
  and demo video links where verified demos exist (never invented).
- Collapses finished sections (accordion cards) so a completed workout stays tidy.
- Times the session with a server-authored deadline, so closing and reopening
  the app resumes the running session with the correct time remaining.
- Supports the full session lifecycle: start, pause, resume, clear, complete,
  and timer expiry, with one source of truth on the server.
- Provides a "Clear session" button with a confirmation step. A session ends
  only on workout completion, timer expiry, or an explicit confirmed Clear --
  never on back navigation or closing the app.
- Shows a sticky status bar and progress bar so the user's place in the session
  is always visible.
- Shows a weekly gym calendar: two fixed gym days plus a configurable third
  day (Friday morning, Friday night, or Saturday morning). Tapping a gym day
  opens that day's session; completed days are logged toward a 3-per-week goal.

## Vision

The exercise catalog is split into a fixed "foundation block" (warm-up,
stability, cool-down) and a rotating "accessory block" (currently loaded
strength work). Future upper-body, back, and arm exercises will slot into the
accessory block without redesigning the app, growing it into a personalized
training companion with more routines and more muscle groups. To add
exercises, edit data/exercises.js.

## Tech stack

- Node.js 18+ with Express (backend) and better-sqlite3 (SQLite database).
- Static frontend in public/ (index.html, styles.css, app.js).
- No accounts, no analytics, no tracking, no personal data. Session identity
  is a random token in an HttpOnly cookie; the database file (data/app.db)
  is gitignored.
- Security rules: the server never trusts client-supplied timer or identity
  values; sessions are scoped per viewer; session rows are deleted on
  completion, expiry, and clear so none accumulate; remaining time is always
  derived from a single server-authored deadline.

## Project layout

- server.js -- Express server: session API, calendar API, settings API.
- data/exercises.js -- exercise catalog: sections, doses, muscle-group tags,
  demo links, foundation/accessory block tags. This is where future exercises
  are added.
- data/app.db -- SQLite database, created automatically at first run.
- public/index.html -- app shell (status bar, timer, routine, calendar).
- public/styles.css -- styles, light/dark aware.
- public/app.js -- frontend logic. Timer state is always read from the
  server; the page never computes timer values locally.
- README.md -- full documentation: features, session lifecycle, quick start,
  API overview.
- package.json -- dependencies (express, better-sqlite3) and start script.

## How to run it

Requirements: Node.js 18 or newer.

1. npm install
2. npm start
3. Open http://localhost:3000

Environment variables: PORT (default 3000), SESSION_MINUTES (default 30,
useful for testing shorter sessions).

## API summary

- GET /api/state -- session (with server-computed remaining time),
  exercises, settings.
- POST /api/session/start -- idempotent start (resumes a paused session).
- POST /api/session/pause -- server snapshots remaining time once.
- POST /api/session/resume -- server re-anchors one fresh deadline.
- POST /api/session/check -- check/uncheck an exercise; completes and logs
  the workout when all are checked.
- POST /api/session/clear -- requires { session_id, confirm: true }.
- GET /api/calendar -- week view with gym days and completions.
- PUT /api/settings -- set the flexible third gym day.

## Safety

This is a workout companion, not medical advice. The app tells users to train
within a comfortable range, that sharp pain is a stop sign, and to follow
their clinician's guidance when training around an injury or condition.
